hypotheses.reasoning: Origin is a Postgres lock held by an idle-in-transaction session (txn 85595, application_name=payment-svc-reconciler) holding RowExclusiveLock on the orders table from ~01:34:46Z (#884). Its transaction never committed or rolled back, so updates to orders queue behind it: postgres reports processes waiting for ShareLock on txn 85595 (#963, #1010). payment-svc's UPDATE on orders then hits statement_timeout (#999, #1089), so POST /charge calls time out at order-service (ReadTimeout / 15s, #1005, #1093). order-service's connection pool to payment-svc saturates (#1174, #1246), and api-gateway returns 504s after 11-29s (#1123, #1225, #1376, #1413). The gateway 504s, pool saturation and queueing are downstream symptoms. Successful checkouts were normal until ~01:34:46, which matches the lock onset. The log does not show why that session stayed idle in transaction. Alternative reading: data_integrity from the invoice_archive checksum violations (#308, #601, #683), which are logged as skipped and do not appear to touch the checkout path.

Invoice archive rows in 2019 partitions violate a checksum constraint and the reconciler logs and skips them. This is real but has no evidence of touching the orders table or checkout, so it is likely a red herring for this alert.

verdict.recommendedAction: Terminate the idle-in-transaction session for txn 85595 (application_name=payment-svc-reconciler) to release the RowExclusiveLock on orders, then confirm blocked UPDATEs drain and checkout 504s recover. Find why the payment-svc reconciler leaves a transaction open, likely a missing commit or rollback on the error path. Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for the reconciler role. Separately investigate the invoice_archive checksum violations in the 2019 partitions. Consider lowering payment-svc statement_timeout or adding a circuit breaker so order-service fails fast instead of queuing.
